ops.title: G1 verdict: internal/trust ships kernel-only; AMFI enforces teamID at exec
ops.body:
GATE G1 (AMFI team-identifier binding measurement) — RESOLVED, ship-as-specified branch.

MEASURED (macOS 26.5.2, real Developer ID Application cert SXKCTF23Q2 from 1Password
OpenClaw/MACOS_SIGN_P12, rcodesign 0.29.0, controlled 3-way trial varying only the CD
teamID string):
  A auto team            -> runs, CS_OPS_VALIDATION_CATEGORY=6, csops teamID=SXKCTF23Q2
  B --team-name SXKCTF23Q2 (correct)  -> runs, category 6, teamID=SXKCTF23Q2
  C --team-name FORGE00000 (forged)   -> codesign --verify "a Team Identifier is wrong or
                                          inappropriate"; exec SIGKILL rc=137, never runs.
B-vs-C (same cert/chain/timestamp/flag, only the team string differs) isolates the team
value as the sole cause. STATUS word on the valid runs = 0x22011311 (CS_VALID | CS_FORCED_LV
| hardened runtime).

WHY THIS SETTLES IT: web research (primary-source xnu read) correctly found the KERNEL's
csblob_parse_teamid() reads teamID as a raw CD string with no certificate cross-check, and
csops(CS_OPS_TEAMID) returns that cached string. The enforcement that closes the hole is one
layer up: exec-time validation of a non-platform Developer ID binary goes amfid ->
Security.framework verifySignature() -> errSecCSBadTeamIdentifier, so AMFI SIGKILLs a
forged-team binary BEFORE it runs. A daemonkit peer verifier only ever reads csops on an
already-running, already-connected peer, which by construction passed the exec gate. Hence a
live category-6 peer CANNOT report a forged foreign team.

DECISION for internal/trust (P1c): ship kernel-only exactly as DESIGN specifies — five
csops_audittoken reads (status -> csposture.Check RequireLibraryValidation; validation
category==6; team identifier; signing identifier; DER entitlements via encoding/asn1 with the
six injection rejections). NO off-handshake cdhash-memoized cert-chain check for the team
clause; the G1 "category-6-with-foreign-team" branch did NOT trigger.

THREAT-MODEL CAVEAT: holds on a SIP-enabled machine (the design's threat model). An attacker
who can set amfi_get_out_of_my_way / disable SIP has already defeated code-signing entirely
and is out of scope. The unconditional same-UID floor remains below everything as the backstop.

Reproducer scripts (secret-free; fetch key material via `op read` at runtime, temp-keychain/
key files deleted on every exit): /tmp/g1/{csprobe.c,det.sh}. Related: investigation fdf4db3
(exonerated); SecCode kernel-only decision note bfc1789.
